bug_semantics: CheckAuth in kernel/model/session.go treats a loopback RemoteAddr as enough to skip access-auth-code, cookie, and token checks and grant RoleAdministrator on /api/system/exit, /api/system/getNetwork, /api/system/getWorkspaceInfo, /assets/*, and /export/*. Those skips sit outside the lock-screen-password gate, so they apply even when an access auth code is configured. The fixed-port reverse proxy forwards to the kernel over loopback without injecting a token and without trusted-proxy client-IP rewrite, so a forwarded request is seen as 127.0.0.1. Direct loopback callers were demonstrated to get admin on those endpoints; remote reachability via the proxy is the same mechanism plus forwarding and was not reproduced end-to-end in the advisory.
flaw_origin: f40ed985e10b0f8391d6c94367cc85b9b5fad6bd (2022-05-26) is the first public commit of kernel/model/session.go and first wrote CheckAuth's RemoteAddr 127.0.0.1 skip for /assets/ (and /history/assets/). Parent e650b8100c22e7fd9b9e28c3866af72e0242784a is a docs-only tree; git cat-file -e PARENT:kernel/model/session.go fails. No finer public history of those lines exists. Later human commits only expanded the same skip (/api/system/exit in ed3a6fcb9ab5403bbcc60db78b4f72ddc765668e; getNetwork/getWorkspaceInfo; /export/) and added the fixed-port proxy in 14dcf78cd957236793b8499b33cc13d43fc84666. The 2026 fix does not rewrite the original introducer.

evidence: Advisory GHSA-3mp7-4rh5-jrv9 / CVE-2026-72809 (bundle GHSA-8wx9-j7j5-h9vp) describes localhost-trust admin bypass in CheckAuth for exit/getNetwork/getWorkspaceInfo/assets/export, plus untrusted fixed-port proxy forwarding. At v3.7.2, CheckAuth sets localhost := util.IsLocalHost(c.Request.RemoteAddr) then grants RoleAdministrator on those prefixes when localhost is true, before cookie/BasicAuth. git blame -L 250,330 v3.7.2 -- kernel/model/session.go attributes the RemoteAddr skip origin to f40ed985e1 (assets) and ed3a6fcb9a (exit). git show f40ed985e10b0f8391d6c94367cc85b9b5fad6bd -- kernel/model/session.go first-adds `if strings.HasPrefix(c.Request.RemoteAddr, "127.0.0.1") && (assets || history/assets)`. git cat-file -e e650b8100c22e7fd9b9e28c3866af72e0242784a:kernel/model/session.go fails. git cat-file -p f40ed985e10b0f8391d6c94367cc85b9b5fad6bd shows author/committer Liang Ding, no AI trailers. Direct fix 9c16e9851f0b5d7ed179e5c2fca15a7724666871 replaces localhost := util.IsLocalHost(c.Request.RemoteAddr) with IsLocalRequest requiring RemoteAddr and ClientIP loopback, SetTrustedProxies([127.0.0.1,::1]), and Rewrite SetXForwarded on the fixed-port proxy. Advisory withdrawn_at is null; CVE record is live.
reasoning: Vulnerability is real (CWE-290 localhost-trust auth bypass on a documented endpoint set; not withdrawn). BIC is the smallest surviving public first-write of the RemoteAddr-as-admin skip: f40ed985e10b0f8391d6c94367cc85b9b5fad6bd, parent tree lacks the file. Endpoint expansions and the later proxy are not the first write of the trust rule the advisory patches. BIC authorship is human (Liang Ding, 2022, no AI markers on the commit object). Fix SHA is the GHSA-3mp7 lock commit. Therefore NOT_AI, not AI_ROOT_CAUSE/AI_CODE_FLAWED.
